notes: §1985:XV.3.2.3 SR3: "Statements appearing outside of the set of debugging sections must not reference procedure-names defined within the set of debugging sections." Every statement's procedure-name reference passes ProcedureTableBuilder.ResolveProcedureOperand into StatementValidation.CheckDeclarativesBoundary, whose first arm refuses (COBOL6946) a target in a section marked IsDebugging (set only for a compiled debugging section) from any section not so marked, with no PERFORM exemption. The witness PERFORMs a debugging paragraph from the main section. Probes at --std 85: GO TO, GO TO DEPENDING, ALTER (both operands), PERFORM of the section, PERFORM THRU, PERFORM TIMES/UNTIL/VARYING, a qualified name, SORT INPUT/OUTPUT and MERGE OUTPUT PROCEDURE from the main portion, and PERFORM from a USE AFTER ERROR section, all refuse; a debugging section PERFORMing another's paragraph and GO TO within itself compile and run; without DEBUGGING MODE the name is undefined. Read 6 (2026-11-14, records-read6): the row had no verdict and no test-ref although its witness existed; the reader read CONFORMS and an independent refuter UPHELD it (op-20261114/out-read6/rd-NN.json and rd-NN-refute.json).

next.reason: 1985: "must not reference procedure-names defined within the set of debugging sections"; 2023: "No debugging sections: the 2023 USE rules cover only file exceptions, BEFORE REPORTING, EC and EO; no FOR DEBUGGING format.". 2023 drops USE FOR DEBUGGING and debugging sections. SR-4 governs declarative references in general (PERFORM only), not debugging sections, so the rule has no counterpart.
